title: Trotxi API health
description: Latency, reliability, responsiveness, memory, dependencies and operations for one Trotxi API service. Source: ops/grafana in mobility-core.

list.name: Deploys
list.expr: count by (service_version) (target_info{job="$job"}) unless count by (service_version) (target_info{job="$job"} offset 5m)

panels.title: Service level: is it up, fast and correct right now?
Availability, 24h
panels.description: Share of requests in the last 24 hours that did not fail with a server error (5xx). Pilot target: 99.5%.

panels.title: Server errors, 5m
panels.description: 5xx responses as a share of all responses over the last 5 minutes. Pages above 2%.

panels.title: Latency p95, 5m
panels.description: 95% of requests finished faster than this over the last 5 minutes.

panels.title: Traffic
panels.description: Requests per second, 5 minute average.

panels.title: Memory (RSS)
panels.description: Resident memory of the busiest instance. Render stops a basic-256mb instance at 256 MB.

panels.title: Event-loop delay p99
panels.description: How long work waits for the single JavaScript thread. High means every request is slow, whatever the route.

panels.title: Oldest unapplied payment
panels.description: How long the oldest Paystack event has waited to be applied. Climbs when the payments job is not draining the inbox; this is the failure that left a paid subscription unapplied for hours.

panels.title: Running version
panels.description: Deployed commit. Two values at once means a deploy is rolling or an old instance is still up.

panels.title: Request latency
panels.description: Percentiles across every route. p99 is the experience of the unluckiest 1 in 100.

targets.expr: label_replace(topk(8, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, http_route) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__rate_interval])))), "http_route", "(no matching route)", "http_route", "")

panels.title: Slowest routes, p95 over the selected range
panels.description: Where to look first when the service is slow. Routes are templates, such as /v1/ops/trips/:id.

targets.expr: label_replace(topk(12, histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, http_route) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job="$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range])))), "http_route", "(no matching route)", "http_route", "")

panels.title: Busiest routes, requests per second over the selected range

targets.expr: label_replace(topk(12, sum by (http_route) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job="$job", instance=~"$instance"}[$__range]))), "http_route", "(no matching route)", "http_route", "")

panels.title: Server errors (5xx) by route
panels.description: Any line here is a bug or an outage in a dependency. Open Explore on Tempo filtered to the route to see the failing request.

targets.expr: label_replace(sum by (http_route, http_response_status_code) (rate(http_server_request_duration_seconds_count{job="$job", instance=~"$instance", http_response_status_code=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval])), "http_route", "(no matching route)", "http_route", "")

panels.title: Refused requests: signed out, forbidden, rate limited
panels.description: 401 signed out, 403 forbidden or passkey needed, 426 app build too old, 429 rate limited. A jump in 426 after raising a build floor, or in 429 from one network, shows here first.

panels.title: Scheduled jobs per hour
panels.description: Runs of the maintenance jobs the GitHub Actions schedule calls. A run counts as failed if any item inside it failed.

panels.title: Responsiveness and saturation: is the service keeping up?
Event-loop utilization
panels.description: Share of time the JavaScript thread is busy. Sustained above 80% means requests queue behind each other.

panels.title: CPU
panels.description: Share of one core. Render basic plans are a fraction of a core.

panels.title: Database connections
panels.description: Anything waiting for a connection means the pool is exhausted and requests are queuing for the database.

panels.title: Database query p95 by statement type
Resident memory against the 256 MB plan limit
panels.description: The number Render enforces. A steady climb that never falls back after garbage collection is a leak.

panels.title: Time spent in garbage collection
panels.description: Share of wall time spent collecting garbage. Rising with memory flat means allocation churn.

panels.title: Outbound call p95 by host
panels.description: Paystack, Google sign-in keys, email, push and storage. Telemetry uploads are excluded.

panels.title: Outbound failures by host
panels.description: Error responses and connection failures from third parties.

panels.title: Payment inbox
panels.description: Age of the oldest Paystack event not yet applied. Above 15 minutes the payments job is not draining it.

panels.title: Oldest unresolved purchase
panels.description: Each unresolved purchase blocks that rider from checking out again.
